text:
ci-bot: [overnight-perf-ci] ALERT: 3 regressions flagged in nightly runtime benchmarks. Suites: latency-kv-prefix, throughput-large-batch, regen-attention. Commits in window: a1b2c3d -> c3d4e5f. Jobs: https://ci.internal/1799 :rotating_light:
eva: copying the CI summary here — which regression should we triage first?
sam: latency-kv-prefix looks highest impact for customer workloads. i'll take that one. can someone post the exact reproduce command?
ci-bot: reproduce: `./tools/run_bench.sh --suite latency-kv-prefix --model redwood-v1 --seq 1024 --commits a1b2c3d..c3d4e5f --runs 5`
jordan: i pushed a patch yesterday touching KV cache eviction heuristics (PR #482). marking as likely suspect.
maria: @jordan which nodes did you test on? we saw reg only on certain GPU types (A100-40 vs A100-80).
jordan: tested on dev A100-40 only. no large-batch runs there.
ryan: i'll run the reproduce + perf record on a100-80 in the morning. command i'll use: `perf record -F 99 -g -- ./bin/runtime_bench --suite latency-kv-prefix --model redwood-v1 --seq 1024` then `perf script | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg`.
sam: thanks @ryan. if you see heavy stacks in runtime::kv::evict or allocator, ping me.
eva: can we get a quick bisect range? smallest blame window would help.
ci-bot: suspected commits touching runtime/kv: a1b2c3d (prev), b2c3d4e (jordan change), c3d4e5f (followup).
maria: i'll pin the canary to a1b2c3d for Dedicated runs to avoid user impact while we triage. deploy change is small, i can do it now. :white_check_mark:
jordan: if bisect confirms my change, i can rework eviction to be less aggressive for long prefix workloads.
sam: also noting throughput-large-batch regression seems unrelated (different kernel path). assigning @eva to coordinate that one?
eva: will take throughput-large-batch — i'll start by comparing kernel selection logs between commits. quick grep: `grep "kernel=matmul" logs/* | sort | uniq -c`
ryan: update: i've started a manual run on a100-80, reproducer completed once, latency median up ~18% vs a1b2c3d. uploading perf data to /artifacts/1799/perf.tar.gz
sam: nice, can you grep for `kv_cache_fill` and `kv_get` in the perf stacks? that's the hypothesis.
ryan: saw a lot of `malloc` + `memcpy` frames attributed to cache reorg; stuck in allocator path. attaching excerpt: ```# perf top excerpt
malloc+0x30
memcpy+0x120
runtime::kv::reorg+0x210
```
maria: that aligns with the eviction heuristic causing copies. @jordan can you flip a flag to disable the aggressive reorg so we can validate impact?
jordan: yes, adding a runtime flag `--kv-reorg-threshold=0` in PR now to test without heuristic. will push in ~15m.
eva: plan summary: 1) @maria pin canary to a1b2c3d, 2) @jordan push flag to disable reorg, 3) @ryan run bench+perf on a100-80 and a100-40, 4) @sam watch latency-kv-prefix results and prepare rollback if needed. check-in in ~60m here.
sam: sounds good. also opened an internal tracking issue: infra/1799. please drop logs there.
eva: thanks everyone — if the disabled reorg brings latency back within 5%, we'll ship a hotfix revert. ping here with results. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: note: auto-retry scheduled for throughput-large-batch on a100-80 at +30m.
ryan: pushed results to infra/1799, perf tar and flame.svg. initial numbers: median latency delta +2% with reorg disabled (on a100-80). will run a100-40 next.
eva: great, leaving this thread open for async updates. we'll consolidate findings in the issue and follow with PR for revert if confirmed.
